# Engineering Notebook

Engineering notes on data systems, AI agents, and the tools built to understand them.
Every project was actually built. Claims are backed by code, tests, or measurements.

Full URL list: https://emanisha.in/sitemap-index.xml

## Projects

- [Autonomous Data Engineer](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/autonomous-data-engineer/): A task-running agent for data work: state machine, nine tools, human approval gates, and full trace replay — how it started, what broke, what was decided, and what the evidence says. [Web & data; Active; stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, PostgreSQL + pgvector, Polars, DuckDB, PySpark, Next.js 13]
- [Data Engineering Mastery Platform](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/data-eng-mastery/): A study coach for data-engineering exams: how it started, what broke, what was decided, and what the evidence says — explained in plain words. [Education / Learning; Active; stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, PostgreSQL + pgvector, Redis, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, Next.js frontend]
- [Learn Marathi](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/learn-marathi/): A 200-page static Marathi learning site synced from a real Flutter curriculum — engineered so every page earns its place in search and funnels readers to the app. [Education / SEO; Active; stack: Astro 7, TypeScript, MDX, Playwright]
- [MF360 Academy](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/mf360-academy/): An AI-native certification prep platform with zero runtime LLM dependency: offline pipeline generates and validates, the website serves pre-built intelligence — architecture, decisions, and an honest early status. [Education; Concept; stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Deterministic study engine, Content store, Offline AI pipeline]
- [MF360: Mutual Fund Intelligence Platform](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/mutual-fund-360/): Trustworthy answers from messy Indian mutual-fund data: methodology first, corrections as rows, golden portfolios as proof. [Finance / FinTech; Active; stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, PostgreSQL 16, Redis, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, Next.js 14]
- [Wealthpath (networth-app)](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/networth-app/): A personal net-worth tracker that refuses to pretend about the future: snapshots as truth, bands instead of point forecasts, honest math. [Finance / FinTech; Active; stack: Next.js 14, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, better-sqlite3, Dexie/IndexedDB, PostgreSQL, React Query, Recharts, Vitest, Playwright]
- [YouTube Automation Agent](https://emanisha.in/notebook/projects/youtube-automation-agent/): An open-source agent that runs a YouTube channel end to end: seven specialist agents, approval-first publishing gates, evidence in SQLite, and growth experiments — how it started, what broke, what was decided, and what the evidence says. [Automation; Active; stack: Node.js 18+, Express, SQLite, LangGraph-style agents, googleapis, FFmpeg, Playwright]

## Tutorials

### Series: data-eng-mastery (https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/)
- [Part 1: Repo structure and the spec-driven method](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/01-repo-and-method/): Follow one learner from signup to study plan while learning how specs, ADRs, and a Makefile keep a year-long build coherent. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Docker]
- [Part 2: The learning engine: how the app knows what Priya needs](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/02-learning-engine/): Six small algorithms decide what she studies, when she reviews, and whether she's ready — real code, hand-worked numbers, zero AI. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, Pytest]
- [Part 3: API and data model: what each endpoint does for Priya](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/03-api-and-data/): Follow her clicks through sixteen router groups: what each API does, where her data lives, and why writes are decided server-side. [difficulty: beginner; tech: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2, Pydantic v2, PostgreSQL]
- [Part 4: The content pipeline: how Priya's curriculum gets built](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/04-content-pipeline/): Follow one syllabus from raw PDF to validated, searchable lesson: seven stages, idempotent re-runs, ordered validators, gated publishing. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, Redis, PostgreSQL]
- [Part 5: Knowledge systems and capstone: search, agents, and principles](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/05-knowledge-capstone/): How Priya finds things, how agents use the same backend, every term defined, and the principles worth stealing — with what I'd investigate next. [difficulty: beginner; tech: PostgreSQL + pgvector, Python 3.11]
- [Part 6: Guided demo: one real hour inside the app](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/data-eng-mastery/06-guided-demo/): Register, tour, practice, and break things on the live build: what works first-hand, what fails, and what each failure teaches. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL]
### Series: learn-marathi (https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/)
- [Part 1: The problem: 200 Marathi lessons that must each earn their place](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/01-problem-and-architecture/): Why Learn Marathi exists, the constraints that shaped it, and the sync-to-static architecture they led to — explained for newcomers. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Astro 7, TypeScript, Node sync scripts]
- [Part 2: One intent per page: what became a page and what didn't](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/02-intent-to-pages/): How search intent and a 15-entry size gate decided every URL — and why 1002 words became zero word-pages. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Astro 7, Markdown datasets]
- [Part 3: The dataset engine: validated content that cannot render lies](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/03-dataset-engine/): How typed datasets, resolvers that throw, and a prebuild QA gate keep 200 pages honest. [difficulty: beginner; tech: TypeScript, Node scripts, Astro content]
- [Part 4: Pages and funnel: a tour from hub to app without dark patterns](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/04-pages-and-funnel/): Every route, the components that render it, and the honest CTA ladder that ends at the app. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Astro 7, MDX components, Formspree]
- [Part 5: Scale without duplication: linking, languages, and images at 200 pages](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/05-scale-without-duplication/): The hard seams: internal linking with no orphans, a Hindi mirror without duplication, and per-page images at scale. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Astro 7, hreflang, OG tooling]
- [Part 6: Capstone: rebuild one slice of the 200-page engine yourself](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/learn-marathi/06-capstone/): Full-flow recap, glossary, testing layers, stealable principles, and a guided exercise. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Astro 7, TypeScript]
### Series: mutual-fund-360 (https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/mutual-fund-360/)
- [Part 1: Method and monolith: how a 383-file project stays coherent](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/mutual-fund-360/01-method-and-monolith/): Follow one investor from CAS upload to reviewed portfolio while learning the doc/ vs docs/ split, task protocol, and DDD layers that keep it coherent. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, FastAPI, PostgreSQL]
- [Part 2: Domain core: frozen entities, masked identity, honest tax](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/mutual-fund-360/02-domain-core/): Build value objects that can't hold invalid states, PAN handling that can't leak, and a tax engine with FY rules — verbatim code included. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, Pytest]
- [Part 3: Money math: XIRR, TER leakage, overlap, and harvesting](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/mutual-fund-360/03-money-math/): Compute what Ravi actually pays and earns: XIRR with fallbacks, regular-vs-direct lifetime cost, overlap flags, and tax-loss harvesting — formulas first. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, Pytest]
- [Part 4: Ingestion: CAS files, deltas, NAVs, and fuzzy matching](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/mutual-fund-360/04-ingestion/): Turn Ravi's messy statements into validated facts: CAS parsing, correction rows, NAV pipeline, and 4-strategy scheme mapping with confidences. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Python 3.11, PostgreSQL, Redis]
- [Part 5: API, security, testing, and capstone](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/mutual-fund-360/05-api-security-testing/): Serve Ravi's data with RLS and masked PANs, prove money math with 24 golden portfolios, and keep the glossary and principles worth stealing. [difficulty: beginner; tech: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Pytest]
### Series: networth-app (https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/)
- [Part 1: The problem: a net-worth tracker that works offline and tells the truth](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/01-problem-and-architecture/): Why Wealthpath exists, the constraints that shaped it, and the architecture they led to — explained for newcomers to web development. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Next.js 14, TypeScript, better-sqlite3, Dexie, PostgreSQL]
- [Part 2: The calculation engine: small math modules you can trust](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/02-implementation/): Eight framework-free modules do every calculation. What pure functions are, what each module computes, and why tested math beats clever math. [difficulty: beginner; tech: TypeScript, Vitest]
- [Part 3: API and persistence: what happens when you click Save](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/03-api-and-persistence/): What an API route is, how 21 of them store your data, why input is validated at the door, and why one file holds the whole database. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Next.js 14, better-sqlite3, Zod]
- [Part 4: Client tour: pages, shared state, and the app shell](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/04-client-tour/): All 15 pages, what shared state holds and why, how forms and charts stay consistent, and what makes the app installable and themed. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Next.js 14, React 18, React Query, Recharts]
- [Part 5: Offline and sync: how the app works with no server](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/05-offline-and-sync/): What offline-first means, the fetch interposer that makes it possible, the browser database mirror, and how cloud sync stays simple and safe. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Dexie, better-sqlite3, PostgreSQL]
- [Part 6: Capstone: the full picture, the vocabulary, the principles](https://emanisha.in/notebook/tutorials/networth-app/06-capstone/): How the layers fit together, every important term defined, how the project is tested, and six principles worth stealing for your own builds. [difficulty: beginner; tech: Vitest, Playwright]

## Writing

- [Agent skills field guide: what to use, where to find them, what to build](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/agent-skills-field-guide/): Anatomy of an agent skill, a checklist mapping tasks to skills from a real inventory, how local skills compare to Claude conventions, and which custom skills are worth building.
- [I Let the Browser Award XP. That Was a Mistake.](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-browser-xp/): The data-eng-mastery app once trusted Priya's browser to award experience points. Browsers can lie. The story of BUG-017: what I assumed, what broke, and why the server owns rewards now.
- [Two Codebases, One Argument: The Dashboard 500 and the Drift Behind It](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-contract-drift/): A dashboard that 500'd on every load, practice feedback showing blanks, a leaderboard that couldn't count — eight contract-drift sites in data-eng-mastery, one missing guardrail.
- [The First Customer Crashed Checkout: Five Paths Nobody Ever Ran](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-dead-code-paths/): A NameError on first subscription, a GDPR delete that selected instead of deleting, a fake export URL, a missing exam column — data-eng-mastery's unexecuted paths, fixed and one still open.
- [Green Tests, Red Services: The Suite Passed and the Backend Still Disagreed](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-green-tests-red-services/): Eighteen failing tests fixed to 86/86 in data-eng-mastery — and the service-layer drift the suite didn't catch: stale columns, duplicate SM-2 math, a canonical module nobody calls.
- [Nobody Could Log In: Four Bugs Wearing a Trenchcoat](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-nobody-could-log-in/): Tokens that were always null, a guard that bounced everyone, a login body that serialized to '{}', and a refresh flow that never fired — the data-eng-mastery auth saga.
- [The Plan Said Done: A Hardening That Exists Mostly as Checkmarks](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-plan-said-done/): A leaked API key still in config, token hardening absent from every branch, pipeline stubs reporting zeros — and the untracked plan file that marks them all done.
- [Two Writes That Silently Discarded You](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/de-silent-writes/): A password change that toasted success and changed nothing, and study sessions that saved zeros — data-eng-mastery's silent-write failures (BUG-006, BUG-008).
- [Postgres for everything: rows, vectors, and text in one store](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/postgres-for-everything/): Implement hybrid content search without new infrastructure: one similarity query, the dimension contract, and an honest split criterion.
- [FastAPI in production: three afternoons to boring reliability](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/production-fastapi/): Move one write server-side, enforce layers with tests, install CI gates — each step grounded in real code from a learning-platform backend.
- [I inventoried 80 projects on my own hard drive](https://emanisha.in/notebook/blog/inventory-80-projects/): How an exclusion-first PowerShell scanner, deterministic scoring, and honest caveats turned 300 GB of accumulated side projects into a triage-able inventory.

## Experiments

- [Exclusion-first traversal cut a filesystem scan by 77%](https://emanisha.in/notebook/experiments/exclusion-first-scan/): Three runs of a PowerShell project-discovery scanner show what happens when virtualenvs and dependency trees are pruned before descending instead of filtered after. [status: Complete; hypothesis: Checking exclusions before descending (rather than filtering results after) removes most of the work in a user-profile scan, because dependency trees dominate directory counts.]
- [Seeded Monte Carlo: determinism check and seed sensitivity](https://emanisha.in/notebook/experiments/seeded-monte-carlo/): Is a seeded wealth-projection engine bit-identical per seed, how far does the median move across seeds, and is 1000 simulations fast enough for the browser? [status: Complete; hypothesis: A seeded LCG-based Monte Carlo engine returns bit-identical results for the same seed, varies only a few percent across seeds, and runs fast enough for client-side use.]
